name: Jonathan Hurst
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Robot Officer, Agility (formerly Agility Robotics); Professor of Robotics, Oregon State University
profile: Carnegie Mellon-trained roboticist (BS, MS, PhD) who joined Oregon State in 2008 and ran its Dynamic Robotics Lab. In 2015 he co-founded Agility Robotics with Damion Shelton and Mikhail Jones to commercialise his legged-locomotion research; its humanoid Digit targets logistics/warehouses. Agility has raised 640M+ USD and is valued around 2.5B USD; renamed Agility in March 2026.
interesting_fact: Agility's robots descend from his lab's spring-mass biped ATRIAS (modelled on how a pogo stick works) and the ostrich-like Cassie, unveiled in 2017 and sold to university research groups, before the humanoid Digit.
deep_cut_fact: He was Oregon State University's first robotics professor (2008); the legged-locomotion program he built grew into an OSU robotics MS/PhD program, which he says was only the third such program in the US.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (RoboBusiness, AI Infra Summit, CMU Yata lecture) and podcast guest - receptive to media. Press contact Tim Smith (Element PR) via media@ address. Title variously listed as CTO in older sources; current is Chief Robot Officer.

name: Valentyn S. Volkov
profile: Physicist specialising in nanophotonics and 2D materials who co-founded XPANCEO in 2021 with entrepreneur Roman Axelrod to build an all-in-one smart contact lens (XR display, health monitoring, night vision, zoom). He leads its R&D team; in July 2025 XPANCEO raised a 250M USD Series A at a 1.35B USD valuation.
interesting_fact: XPANCEO's scientific advisory board is chaired by Nobel laureate Sir Konstantin Novoselov, co-discoverer of graphene.
deep_cut_fact: Before XPANCEO he directed MIPT's Center for Photonics and 2D Materials, and co-authored a 2020 Laser & Photonics Reviews study proposing quantum dots above graphene to convert light into surface waves with a calculated efficiency of up to ~90% (vs. under 10% for prior schemes).
notes: Regular AWE XR conference speaker. hello@ is a general company inbox. Founding year given as 2018 in one article; most sources say 2021.

name: Xavier Orr
current_role: Founder, Anitron (humanoid robot AI); board director & advisor, Advanced Navigation
profile: UWA mechatronics/computer science graduate who co-founded Advanced Navigation with Chris Shaw in 2012, commercialising his AI-based inertial navigation algorithm; the Sydney firm (valued ~1B USD) makes navigation systems for drones, ships, satellites and a lunar lander. He stepped down as co-CEO in July 2024, remains a director, and founded Anitron to build 'brains' for humanoid robots.
interesting_fact: He dropped out of his PhD to start the company, reasoning that publishing would give away his secrets and the university would own part of the IP; he and Shaw started on personal loans and maxed credit cards in Shaw's Subiaco garage and were profitable within nine months.
deep_cut_fact: A UWA lecturer, Dr Adrian Keating, steered him toward neural networks as an undergrad; his 2009 final-year thesis, a neural-network algorithm for physics applications, showed a tenfold performance gain and became the basis of Advanced Navigation.
notes: Stepped back from Advanced Navigation for a family matter (do not raise). Anitron (pre-seeded 1M USD by Orr; Unitree G1-based beta trials, shirt-folding demo) is the most current topic. No Anitron contact found.
